newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka rupee stalled, dealers await direction.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka rupee stalled, dealers await direction.

text.p: The Sri Lanka rupee was untraded nearly two hours after the session began, as banks waited to see which way the dollar-rupee exchange would go after the Central Bank pushed down the U.S. unit marginally, dealers said.
The rupee was quoted at its opening level of 56.69 to the dollar at 0430 GMT. The rupee closed at 56.70 on Tuesday.
"There is some commercial demand and short covering waiting in the wings, but we want to see which way the dollar will go," said an American Express Bank dealer.
The Central Bank drove the dollar down by half a local cent, responding to the dollar's weakness against the yen and mark, dealers said.
Overnight call money was well offered and trading at 13.75 percent after opening at 14, dealers said.
"The Central Bank cut the overnight repurchase rate to 12.75 percent from 13, giving an indication of how liquid the overnight call market is," said a Standard Chartered dealer.
